Day 3 - 1st water change

April 24, 2026

I perform my first water change, about 30%. Pumping out the water uprooted my weak (ovalis?) in the back right corner, which I’ve been having trouble planting. With the lower...

I perform my first water change, about 30%. Pumping out the water uprooted my weak (ovalis?) in the back right corner, which I’ve been having trouble planting. With the lower water level, a pond-like smell becomes prominent. I scoop out the floating sediment best I can with a measuring cup and wipe away the dirt clinging to the sides of the tank. I snip and remove a dying leaf from the crypt. 5 snails now.

week1

Day 2 - SNAIL DISCOVERY

April 23, 2026

14 salvinia. SNAIL DISCOVERY ! I discover another smaller one later in the day. I also saw some small white worms that Google and Reddit say are likely detritus worms....

14 salvinia. SNAIL DISCOVERY ! I discover another smaller one later in the day. I also saw some small white worms that Google and Reddit say are likely detritus worms. The red stem plant in the middle seems to be doing well. I plant my remaining eligible clippings.

I notice biofilm forming at the surface of the water. There’s a lot of floating sediment now too. My friend points out wispy hair algae emerging from the leaves of my plants. I’m definitely doing a water change as soon as I can tomorrow.

A couple hours before the pickup time, I’m wandering Marshall’s for possible tank backings or levelling materials. I didn’t realize this location was closing down. I pick through some drying mats, but can’t picture any of them looking good around the tank. The tank has a thin one built in anyway, so it’s more for peace of mind.

We’re meeting at the Jewel by the Orange Line, and I get there early enough to do some grocery shopping. The layout of this store vaguely resembles the local Kroger back home in Michigan. I’m just about to check out when I get a message
